spec.description: Fetch one work: the book itself, above any particular edition of it.

work_id.description: Work id, the last segment of a work key: `OL893414W` for `/works/OL893414W`.

response.title: Work
response.description: One work record, as its editors have built it. Most fields are optional because a record grows one edit at a time.

key.description: The work's own key, such as `/works/OL893414W`.

authors.description: Who wrote it, each as a pointer to an author record plus the role they played.

items.title: WorkAuthor
items.description: One author's part in this work.

description.description: What the book is about. A plain string on some records and a `TextValue` on others: Open Library's editors have written both, and the API returns whichever is stored.

links.description: External links editors attached to the work.

revision.description: Revision number of the record as served.

latest_revision.description: Highest revision number the record has.

unverified.detail: Written from the Open Library documentation and the live endpoint's own shape, with no recording committed yet. The Record workflow replays `examples/*.request.json` through a client generated from this spec and fills in the responses.

notes: `description` is genuinely two shapes -- a bare string, or `{"type": "/type/text", "value": ...}` -- so it is an `anyOf` of both. A spec that picked one would fail on half the catalogue.

`first_publish_date` is served on many works and is not declared here. Its values are free-form human text (`1965`, `October 1965`, `1965-10-01`), so there is no wire format to declare, and typing it as a date would promise a conversion that fails. Read it off an unvalidated response, or add it as a plain string with a note if a caller needs it.

Open Library serves editions from `/books/<edition_id>.json` and resolves an ISBN through `/isbn/<isbn>.json`, which answers with a redirect. Neither is specced here: the redirect is a transport behaviour a core has to opt into, and an edition record is a different shape again.
